thread:
sara (AcmeClient): hey team — after your deploy around ~11:03 UTC today our prompt templates that used to be stable are now failing intermittently. small spacing/punctuation changes that used to be fine now return garbage or a 502. example: template A worked yesterday, now returns 'N/A' or a truncated text. hitting production, customers blocked.

maya (support): hi @sara, sorry for the disruption — can you paste the exact template and a sample input that reproduces? are you seeing 502s or model output quality regressions (weird completions)?

sara (AcmeClient): both. 502 for ~10% requests, and when no 502 the output is wrong. quick repro: ``
PROMPT_TEMPLATE="Summarize the following release notes in one short sentence:\n\n{{release_notes}}"
INPUT="Release notes: Fixed crash in auth flow. Minor performance bumps. "
``
previously: "Fixed crash in auth flow; small perf improvements."
now: "N/A" or sometimes "Fixed crash in auth" (truncated). curl: ``curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"redwood-2027-beta","prompt":"'$PROMPT_TEMPLATE'","variables":{"release_notes":"'$INPUT'"}}'``

maya (support): thanks — can you confirm which model alias you were pinned to before? any chance you switched to a beta alias?

sara (AcmeClient): we were on alias `redwood-stable` pinned by customer settings. nothing changed on our side. your docs show a deploy today: saw an email about a runtime update.

deploy-bot: canary -> stable rollout completed: id=rollout-20270512-1103, started=2027-05-12T11:03:00Z, finished=2027-05-12T11:18:22Z

devon (eng-ml): pinging in. thanks @maya + @sara for the repro. early hypothesis: a prompt preprocessor or tokenizer change in the new runtime variant may be collapsing whitespace or altering how template variables are escaped, which would cause very brittle templates. also possible: a change to prefix trimming in the model input path.

liam (eng-runtime): we did push a patch that normalizes consecutive whitespace (to reduce token variance) in the request pipeline — the intent was to improve caching and batching. rollout id matches deploy-bot above. devon, could that normalization break semantics for templates that rely on exact spacing/punctuation?

devon (eng-ml): yes — if templates rely on double newlines or precise spacing for instruction separation, normalizing could merge sections and cause the model to interpret differently. it's a known edge case.

chris (eng-sre): ops note: we also saw a small uptick in 502s for the same rollout in regions-us-east-1 between 11:05 and 11:22 UTC. 502s correlate with increased tail latency on model instances under batching windows that changed slightly after the patch. logs attached below.

chris (eng-sre): ``[2027-05-12T11:12:04Z] connection reset by peer: model-worker-23, 502 for request id=abc123``

maya (support): immediate mitigation options: (1) pin affected customers to previous runtime variant (rollback for their traffic), (2) disable whitespace normalization for them via feature-flag, (3) rollback full rollout if impact is large. @devon @liam recommendations?

liam (eng-runtime): we can feature-flag the normalizer per-tenant quickly. rollout change is non-breaking for most customers, but we should enable a per-tenant opt-out and flip AcmeClient back to old behavior while we patch. I'll open a ticket to flip their flag and route their API key to the pre-normalizer path.

devon (eng-ml): agree with opt-out. we should also run the customer prompt set through our internal test suite against the new runtime to reproduce. if reproduces, we add a preprocessor transform that preserves double-newline separators and common template delimiters like `{{...}}`.

maya (support): @sara — we're going to opt you out of whitespace normalization now and rerun your requests in canary. I'll DM you for the API key and confirm when done. is that okay? :pray:

sara (AcmeClient): yes please, thanks. the customer is on a support call, they're breathing easier if we can at least get the traffic stable.

chris (eng-sre): action items assigned:
- liam: flip tenant feature-flag for AcmeClient to disable normalizer (ETA 10m)
- devon: run customer prompt set through internal regression harness + produce minimal failing diff (ETA 30m)
- maya: keep customer updated and collect 3 failing examples (ETA 15m)

liam (eng-runtime): done — flag flipped for tenant `acct-acme-111`. routing shows their requests go to pre-normalizer path now.

maya (support): @sara can you re-run the curl above and paste the raw response?

sara (AcmeClient): re-tested after the flip, output now matches previous behaviour — no more "N/A" or truncation. no 502s in the 20 requests we made. thank you.

devon (eng-ml): good — I'm running the full prompt set now. initial diff shows this minimal root cause: our normalizer collapsed consecutive newlines and removed a trailing space inside `{{release_notes}}` which changed token alignment causing truncation after the first sentence in some cases. I'll prepare a patch that preserves "\n\n" pairs and token-safe trimming around mustache delimiters.

liam (eng-runtime): we'll ship the fix behind the normalizer flag and enable it by default only after we pass the prompt regression suite. also adding a canary rule to run customer template suites during canary phase so we catch customers that rely on exact spacing.

maya (support): I'll keep this thread updated with the customer's notes from the call and confirm when we re-enable normalization. for now the immediate customer impact is mitigated. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sara (AcmeClient): thanks so much — appreciate the fast response.

deploy-bot: incident monitoring: regression alert closed for tenant acct-acme-111 at 2027-05-12T11:42:10Z

chris (eng-sre): postmortem next steps: add automated test that includes common template patterns (mustache, handlebars, double-newline separators) to the canary gating; add metric alert for jump in template-failure-rate per-tenant.

maya (support): assigning follow-ups:
- devon: patch and PR to normalizer preserving template semantics (link forthcoming)
- liam: add per-tenant opt-out dashboard and canary gating rule
- chris: create alert for template-failure-rate and tie to oncall playbook

maya (support): closing thread here once PR merged and we re-enable for AcmeClient with green test results.

sara (AcmeClient): confirmed — will reopen if we see anything else. thanks again!
